item.title: security: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft describes an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonated executives and used fake invoices to target finance teams for ACH payment fraud. The post focuses on the attack pattern and how organizations can protect against it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft Defender is described as detecting and disrupting AI-themed phishing, malware, and multi-stage attacks across the attack chain. The post is a Microsoft Security Blog entry dated 2026-09-10.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
Microsoft reports that invisible Unicode characters, previously used in AI prompt injection, are now being used to hide words from email filters as part of phishing evasion. The technique relies on obfuscating text before parsers process it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Counterfeit installers to system compromise: Tracking a deceptive software download campaign
item.description:
Microsoft describes an active malware campaign that uses fake software download pages and repackaged installer archives to impersonate legitimate vendors. The post includes observed tactics, Defender XDR detections, indicators of compromise, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
item.description:
Microsoft reports that Q2 2026 saw continued declines in several phishing techniques after disruption of the Tycoon2FA platform. Attackers shifted toward Teams-based social engineering and more automated, multi-stage attack chains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
